Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old female with a few days of dry, itchy rash on hands and arms after swimming; no fever or systemic symptoms reported.
- Clinical impression: dermatitis likely irritant/contact; management includes emollients, topical corticosteroid option, and OTC antihistamines; follow-up in 1 week. Stress at work discussed as potential contributing factor.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute dermatitis (dry, itchy rash) on hands and arms. Onset: started a few days ago after swimming. Associated symptoms: redness; no fever, no vomiting, no chest/abdominal symptoms; no spread to chest/legs/face; no sores reported. Temporary failure of coconut butter to relieve symptoms.
- Context: Recent swimming as potential trigger; weather possibly contributing; stress at work discussed.
- Social history/Medications/Examination: Lives alone; primary school teacher; non-smoker; no alcohol; currently taking Microgynon; no prior skin problems reported.
- Plan/Differential: Likely dermatitis; provide patient information leaflet; topical corticosteroid cream (dose/route/frequency not documented) and emollients; OTC antihistamines (Piriton or Loratadine) for itch (dose/route/frequency not documented); paracetamol not helpful (dose/route/frequency not documented); arrange follow-up in 1 week if symptoms persist or worsen.

Issue 2:
- Stress/work-related fatigue. Timeline: past few days; described as being under significant work stress (long hours, challenging students).
- Social history/Examination: Occupation as teacher; lives alone; non-smoker; no alcohol; no other physical symptoms documented.
- Plan/Differential: Acknowledge psychosocial contribution to symptoms; no specific treatment documented in this encounter beyond recognition.

Issue 3:
- Current medications and allergies. 
- Medications: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Lactose intolerance (patient report).
- Additional notes: Family history of asthma (father) and hay fever (mother); no other skin history reported.
- Plan: No changes specified beyond documentation.

Medications:
- Microgynon — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Piriton (chlorpheniramine) — dose/route/frequency not documented (OTC option).
- Loratadine — dose/route/frequency not documented (OTC option).
- Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented (not recommended in this consult).
- Topical corticosteroid cream — dose/route/frequency not documented (as a treatment option).
- Emollients — dose/route/frequency not documented (treatment option).

Allergies:
- Lactose intolerance.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses reported.
- No prior dermatologic history (eczema/dermatitis) noted.
- Not currently taking medications other than Microgynon.

Social History:
- Lives alone; primary school teacher.
- Non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; no recreational drugs.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or objective examination findings documented; no examination performed due to reliance on history.

Plan:
- Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis.
- Recommend topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation and emollients for dry skin.
- Suggest OTC antihistamines (Piriton or Loratadine) for itch.
- Paracetamol not recommended for this presentation.
- If no improvement in several days, return for re-evaluation in 1 week.
